patients.label: Previously healthy 12-year-old female with a left adnexal mass and later chickenpox

identity_evidence.quote: We report a tubo-ovarian abscess as an initial presentation of chickenpox in a 12-year-old female

attribution_limitations: The case-presentation segments describe a left adnexal mass lesion (suspected ovarian tumor, then isolated tubal torsion) and never use the word abscess; the tubo-ovarian abscess diagnosis is stated in the abstract and discussion without a stated diagnostic basis. No aspiration, culture or organism is reported.

The mass volumes conflict: the case text says the repeated ultrasound showed an increase from 27 cc to 40 cc and cites Figure 3A, while the Figure 3A caption gives 16 cc after 2 weeks and the Figure 1 caption gives 40 cc for the ultrasound it shows (cited for the initial ultrasound). The timing of the repeated ultrasound is not stated.

The text says the follow-up ultrasound ten days post discharge showed a volume of 13 cc, while the Figure 3 caption gives 16 cc after 2 weeks and 13 × 16 × 24 mm (3 cc) at 6 weeks; the reference points for the caption times "after 2 weeks" and "6 weeks later" are not stated.

The case text says the internal tubular structure exhibits peripheral enhancement and the mass is surrounded by enhancing soft tissue, while the Figure 2 caption says the mass shows no enhancement post-contrast.
The source writes "the patients" for the single patient (scheduled for surgery; started to have skin lesions); only one patient is described.
The time of the vital signs, anthropometry and laboratory tests is not stated beyond the preceding sentence "Upon presentation, the child appeared acutely ill."
B-HCG is reported as 5 mIU/ml with a stated normal non-pregnant value of less than 5 mIU/ml, while the authors call all tumor markers negative.
